description: A distribution platoon leader must finalize a single-lift manifest for four cargo lots, assign the lots between two trucks, set the dispatch time and medical receiving window, and record the operational controls needed for the movement.

shared_context.S1: The single lift must move four cargo lots without splitting or omitting any lot: Medical, Repair Parts, Water, and Signal Batteries. Each complete lot must be assigned to exactly one truck.
shared_context.S2: Truck 1 and Truck 2 each have a normal rated capacity of 8 pallets, but the final manifest must use each truck's current approved capacity rather than assuming both normal ratings remain available.
shared_context.S3: The standard manifest contains exactly 4 pallets of Repair Parts, 5 pallets of Water, and 2 pallets of Signal Batteries, for 11 pallets before the Medical lot is added; the Medical lot quantity is confirmed on the warehouse release.
shared_context.S4: Both trucks will depart through the East Gate, and the earliest planned dispatch time is 0800.
shared_context.S5: Lt. Morgan signs the final manifest and dispatch instruction. At the daily distribution sync, the warehouse, motor pool, signal, and gate-control leads report current changes before the manifest is signed.
shared_context.S6: The manifest is valid only when every lot stays whole, all four lots are assigned, and the pallet totals on the two trucks fit their approved capacities; once the Medical quantity and any truck restriction are confirmed, the total-pallet and total-capacity arithmetic must balance with no unassigned or split pallets.
shared_context.S7: For this lift, the only valid whole-lot assignment that balances the 14-pallet total against the approved 8-pallet and 6-pallet capacities while placing Signal Batteries on Truck 2 is Truck 1 carrying Medical and Water, and Truck 2 carrying Repair Parts and Signal Batteries. The manifest validation step must reject any assignment that puts more than 8 pallets on Truck 1 or more than 6 pallets on Truck 2.
shared_context.S8: The route timing between East Gate and the Medical receiving point is already assessed as sufficient for a 0930 dispatch to meet the 1000-1100 receiving window, so no additional transit-time confirmation is required before signing.

PF1.text: Sgt. Patel confirmed this morning that the Medical lot is exactly 3 pallets and has a receiving appointment from 1000 to 1100; the receiving confirmation is on the warehouse release but has not yet been added to the distribution brief.

PF2.text: SFC Romero's tire inspection found that Truck 2 must be held to a maximum of 6 pallets for this lift; the restriction is in the motor-pool inspection log but has not been sent to the distribution desk.

PF3.text: Lt. Okafor confirmed that the Signal Batteries require the fixed upright rack installed only in Truck 2; the equipment-custody note is still being reconciled and is not on the current manifest slide.

PF4.text: Sgt. Brooks received a gate-control notice that the East Gate will be closed from 0800 to 0930 for a scheduled inspection; the traffic board has not yet been updated with the closure, so the trucks cannot dispatch through East Gate before 0930.

acceptance_conditions: Truck 1 must carry the Medical and Water lots.
Truck 2 must carry the Repair Parts and Signal Batteries lots.
The Medical lot must be recorded as exactly 3 pallets.
The Medical receiving window must be 1000-1100.
The manifest must include a Truck 2 six-pallet restriction control.
The manifest must include an upright-rack verification for the Signal Batteries.
The dispatch instruction must include East Gate clearance confirmation.
The Medical appointment fact must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C2: ('Signal Batteries' in decisions['truck2_load'] or 'Signal Batteries (2 pallets)' in decisions['truck2_load']) and ('Repair Parts' in decisions['truck2_load'] or 'Repair Parts (4 pallets)' in decisions['truck2_load'])
content_checks.C6: any('Truck 2' in c['detail'] and ('6-pallet' in c['detail'] or '6 pallet' in c['detail'] or 'maximum of 6' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('Truck 2' in c['detail'] and ('upright rack' in c['detail'] or ('rack' in c['detail'] and 'Signal Batteries' in c['detail']) or ('Signal Batteries' in c['detail'] and 'assigned' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('East Gate' in c['detail'] and ('0930' in c['detail'] or '0800' in c['detail']) and ('closure' in c['detail'] or 'closed' in c['detail'] or 'clear' in c['detail'] or 'reopens' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed 3-pallet Medical quantity and 1000-1100 receiving appointment set the Medical load detail, receiving window, and the load placement needed to fit the full 14-pallet manifest.
Truck 2's exact 6-pallet maximum forces its load to the 4-pallet Repair Parts lot plus the 2-pallet Signal Batteries lot and requires the payload restriction control.
The fact that only Truck 2 has the required upright rack fixes the Signal Batteries assignment and requires a rack or assignment verification in the manifest commitment.
The exact 0800-0930 East Gate closure makes the earliest feasible dispatch 0930 and requires a commitment documenting clearance after the closure.
